## Invariants over repeated updates {#sec-ch13-invariants}

The 2603 checks use the existing chapter 6 A-to-B reaction card and chapter 4
water-condensation card. The committed `invariants/README.md` defines inputs,
system boundaries, normalization and the source-mutation protocol.

```bash
python invariants/check_invariants.py --output invariants-result.json
python invariants/inventory_guards.py .reproduce/sources/kintera --check
```

The reaction check executes 1000 implicit steps of 0.001 s. An exactly absent
reactant must give an exactly zero rate; every species amount must remain
nonnegative, without an epsilon or post-step clamp. A second cell undergoes
nonzero conversion. The condensation case performs 1000 closed-volume UV
projections, beginning with supersaturated water; these are equilibrium
projections, not kinetic timesteps. No heat, work, transport or material source
is imposed. Atom totals and independent internal energy must drift by at most
1e-12 of their initial scales on **each** update. Total accumulated drift is
reported separately; it is not divided by 1000 to obtain a pass.

The source guard inventory includes full-SHA links and explicit coverage gaps.
Its separate `--require-effects` gate remains failing until each candidate is
classified and supported by effect or non-reachability evidence.
Passing these two decks does not establish non-reachability of a guard in the
rest of the report, or validate GPU execution. Existing figure baselines and
chapter-owner findings remain unchanged.

The input cards come from @sec-ch06-implicit and @sec-ch04-equilibrate-uv.
The energy oracle uses each card's constant heat capacities and reference
energies, independently of native energy evaluation. The relative drift of an
individual update is its budget change divided by the initial nonzero atom
total, or by the initial sum of absolute energy contributions. This avoids a
small difference of large energy terms in the normalization.

| source | absent-reactant rate | minimum amount (mol/m³) | outcome |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| pre-#151, `53f3ffcc6fefd34513dc04214d506103b2d917ed` | 1e-300 | -9.990009990010119e-301 | fails |
| current, `e357792d50639d68e9090b542edf038d2b029aa2` | 0 | 0 | passes |

: Exact-zero and positivity measurements after 1000 implicit steps. {#tbl-ch13-invariants-zero}

The current-source maximum relative atom drift per reaction step is
2.220446049250313e-16; the maximum relative energy drift per condensation
projection is 9.032488358547774e-16. Both are below 1e-12. These results are
CPU binary64 measurements, not a guarantee for other decks or devices.
Actual-source break builds make the same checks fail: restoring the kinetics
floor produces negative amounts; removing product production gives an atom
budget error of 9.990009990009652e-4 per step; removing the cloud reference-energy
term gives an energy error of 0.1655127589519766 per step. The committed
`invariants/RESULTS.md` and JSON preserve all old/new values and source patches.
